subject: science
title: Guitar Strings Make Sound
objective: Describe how vibrating guitar strings make sound and how to protect our ears.
introduction: Milo plucks a guitar string and hears a sound. How does the string make sound, and how can Maxine protect her ears?

vocabulary.definition: A quick back-and-forth movement that can make sound.
A vibration that travels through air or another material to your ears.
Ways to protect your ears from sounds that are too loud.

items.prompt: Maxine plucks a guitar string and sees it shake. What makes the sound?
items.explanation: The plucked string moves back and forth. That vibration makes the sound; the other objects do not vibrate to make a sound in this scene.

items.prompt: Milo stands near a very loud speaker. Which action protects his hearing?

options.text: Turn the volume all the way up

items.explanation: Very loud sound can hurt ears, so moving away reduces the sound reaching them. The other actions do not make loud listening safer.

items.prompt: Milo reads four claims about sound. Which one is NOT true?
items.explanation: Sound needs matter, such as air, to carry its vibrations, so it cannot travel through a perfect vacuum. Strings and speakers vibrate, and air can carry sound.

items.prompt: A learner plucks a guitar string. What starts the sound?
items.explanation: The string shakes back and forth quickly, and that vibration starts the sound. Color, shadow, and stillness do not make the string sound.

items.prompt: Maxine listens to music through headphones. Which choice is safest?

options.text: Press the speaker against an ear
Listen for hours without a break
Lower the volume and take breaks

items.explanation: Lower volume is gentler on ears and taking breaks helps protect hearing. Maximum volume and pressing speakers close can cause harm.
